quizName: DMV Practice Test #4 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: How do you make the shortest and safest stop on a motorcycle?

options.text: Use only the rear brake.
Use only the front brake.
Let the front tire lock up.
Use both the front and rear brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both the front and rear brakes.
questions.explanation: Use both brakes smoothly and gradually to stop safely and quickly. Do not let either tire skid.

questions.question: When should you do a pre-ride inspection?

options.text: Before every ride.
Once a week.
Once a month.
Twice a month.

questions.correctAnswerText: Before every ride.
questions.explanation: Check your motorcycle before each ride. This only takes a few minutes and helps you avoid problems on the road.

questions.question: What should you do before riding an unfamiliar motorcycle?

options.text: Ride it the same way you ride your own bike, since all bikes are similar.
Check the controls and shift pattern.
Trust the owner that everything works fine.
Assume you know where all the controls are.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check the controls and shift pattern.
questions.explanation: Every motorcycle is different. Learn the controls and gear pattern before riding. Test the throttle, clutch, and brakes a few times first.

questions.question: What should you do when riding on a slippery surface?

options.text: Ride faster than normal.
Use only the front brake.
Slow down.
Use only the rear brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, reduce your speed. Use both brakes and avoid sudden movements.

questions.question: How does riding with a passenger affect a motorcycle?

options.text: It usually makes no difference in how the motorcycle handles.
It is usually safe for new riders.
It can change how the motorcycle handles.
It helps new riders get used to different situations.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can change how the motorcycle handles.
questions.explanation: A passenger adds weight, which changes how the motorcycle handles. Only experienced riders should carry passengers.

questions.question: Why is alcohol different from food and drinks?

options.text: Alcohol reaches the brain within minutes and starts to affect you right away.
Your body never removes alcohol.
It takes a long time to feel alcohol's effects.
Your body gets rid of alcohol very quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Alcohol reaches the brain within minutes and starts to affect you right away.
questions.explanation: Alcohol does not need to be digested, so it enters your blood quickly and reaches your brain within minutes. Your body removes about one drink per hour.

questions.question: What can happen if you take a turn too fast?

options.text: It is safe as long as you stay under the speed limit.
It is safer on a motorcycle than in a car.
It is safe as long as no other vehicles are nearby.
You may end up in another lane or leave the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may end up in another lane or leave the road.
questions.explanation: Taking a turn too fast is dangerous. You may lose control and end up in another lane or off the road. Always slow down for turns.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT required on a DOT-compliant helmet?

options.text: An outer shell that resists impact.
An inner liner that absorbs impact.
A chinstrap that stays secure.
Bright colors painted on it.

questions.correctAnswerText: Bright colors painted on it.
questions.explanation: DOT-compliant helmets must have an impact-resistant outer shell, an impact-absorbing inner liner, a comfort liner, and a secure chinstrap. Bright colors are not required.

questions.question: Where should your feet be when riding a motorcycle?

options.text: Dragging on the ground.
Pointed downward.
Firmly on the footrests.
Away from the controls.

questions.correctAnswerText: Firmly on the footrests.
questions.explanation: Keep your feet firmly on the footrests for balance. Do not drag them or point your toes down, as they could catch on the road. Keep your feet near the controls so you can reach them quickly if needed.

questions.question: What should you do before riding an unfamiliar motorcycle?

options.text: Check that the seat is comfortable.
Assume the motorcycle is in good condition.
Test the throttle, clutch, and brakes a few times.
Ride it the way you normally do, since most bikes are the same.

questions.correctAnswerText: Test the throttle, clutch, and brakes a few times.
questions.explanation: Every motorcycle is different. Get familiar with it before you ride. Learn the gear pattern and test the throttle, clutch, and brakes a few times first.

questions.question: Before riding your motorcycle, you should do all of the following except:

options.text: Check that the headlight works.
Check the oil level.
Test both brake controls to make sure the brake light turns on.
Make sure the paint has no scratches.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure the paint has no scratches.
questions.explanation: Before riding, check your tire pressure and condition. Check your oil and fluid levels. Make sure your headlight, taillight, signal lights, and brake light all work.

questions.question: When passing parked cars, a motorcycle rider should be ready for:

options.text: Empty parking spaces.
A parked car to suddenly pull out into traffic.
Parking meters.
Other drivers to see you and stay out of your way.

questions.correctAnswerText: A parked car to suddenly pull out into traffic.
questions.explanation: When passing parked cars, be ready for one to pull out suddenly. It is safest to ride on the left side of your lane when passing parked cars on your right. This gives you more space to avoid any hazards.

questions.question: If your shoes have laces, you should:

options.text: Tuck them in.
Let them hang loose.
Remove them from your shoes.
Glue them together.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tuck them in.
questions.explanation: Tuck in your shoelaces securely when riding so they do not catch on your motorcycle.

questions.question: Motorcycles have blind spots like cars. When changing lanes, you should:

options.text: Turn your head and look over your shoulder to check your blind spot.
Only look at your mirrors.
Rely on your side vision.
Slow down so any vehicle in your blind spot can pass you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head and look over your shoulder to check your blind spot.
questions.explanation: Blind spots are areas you cannot see in your mirrors. Turn your head and look over your shoulder before you change lanes to check for vehicles.

questions.question: An advantage of keeping a small group of riders is:

options.text: A small group stays together better in traffic than a large group.
A small group can ignore traffic laws to stay together.
Riders will always try to catch up to the group.
It will be hard to keep track of where everyone is.

questions.correctAnswerText: A small group stays together better in traffic than a large group.
questions.explanation: A small group is easier for other vehicles to pass. A small group is less likely to get separated by traffic or traffic lights. Slower riders do not need to rush to catch up.

questions.question: Keeping space around your motorcycle helps you:

options.text: React to hazards.
Hide from other drivers.
Avoid missing hazards.
Look at road signs.

questions.correctAnswerText: React to hazards.
questions.explanation: Keep space around your motorcycle at all times. This gives you time to react if another driver makes a mistake. You will have room to maneuver safely.

questions.question: What material provides the best protection for motorcycle riders?

options.text: Leather
Wool
Polyester
Silk

questions.correctAnswerText: Leather
questions.explanation: Leather provides the best protection for motorcycle riders. Wear clothing made of leather that covers your arms and legs completely.

questions.question: Most crashes happen during daylight. Because of this, you should:

options.text: Not ride during the day.
Wear bright clothing at all times.
Ride on the shoulder to stay out of traffic.
Wear dark clothing at all times.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wear bright clothing at all times.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen during daylight hours. Wear bright-colored clothing when riding so other drivers can see you, even during the day.

questions.question: A danger of riding next to parked cars is:

options.text: You may not find a parking spot.
A driver may pull out suddenly into your path.
Other drivers may be driving slowly looking for a spot.
The road may be uneven.

questions.correctAnswerText: A driver may pull out suddenly into your path.
questions.explanation: Riding next to parked cars is dangerous. A driver might pull out without looking. Car doors might open into your lane. People might step out from between cars.

questions.question: When approaching an uneven surface like a bump or pothole, rise slightly off your seat:

options.text: So you can jump off if needed.
So your legs can absorb the shock.
So other drivers can see you better.
So you can see the uneven surface better.

questions.correctAnswerText: So your legs can absorb the shock.
questions.explanation: When riding over uneven surfaces, rise off your seat so your legs can absorb the impact. This helps prevent the impact from throwing you off the motorcycle.

questions.question: Which fabric gives motorcyclists the most protection?

options.text: Leather
Denim
Polyester
Wool

questions.correctAnswerText: Leather
questions.explanation: Leather jackets and pants offer the best protection when riding a motorcycle.

questions.question: How can you make your motorcycle more visible?

options.text: Add extra lights to your motorcycle.
Do not use your turn signal.
Wear dark clothing.
Wave at people.

questions.correctAnswerText: Add extra lights to your motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Wear bright or reflective clothing to be more visible. Add extra lights, use turn signals, and flash your brake light when needed. These actions help other drivers see you.

questions.question: When should you use a turn signal?

options.text: When you plan to go faster.
Only when there is heavy traffic.
Every time you change lanes.
Only when it is dark.

questions.correctAnswerText: Every time you change lanes.
questions.explanation: Use your turn signal every time you turn or change lanes, even if you think no one is watching.

questions.question: Why is space between your motorcycle and other vehicles important?

options.text: It gives you time to react if another driver makes a mistake.
It keeps you in one spot in the lane with limited movement.
It lets you depend on other drivers to spot hazards.
It requires you to drive faster to keep up with traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: It gives you time to react if another driver makes a mistake.
questions.explanation: Keeping space around your motorcycle gives you time and room to react safely if another driver makes a mistake.

questions.question: Experienced riders use the SIPDE system to make safe decisions. What does SIPDE stand for?

options.text: Scan, Identify, Predict, Decide, and Execute
Speed, Inadvertent, Project, Determine, and Eliminate
Slow, Interpret, Police, Deal, and Extra
Space, Immerse, Pedal, Deal, and Early

questions.correctAnswerText: Scan, Identify, Predict, Decide, and Execute
questions.explanation: SIPDE stands for Scan, Identify, Predict, Decide, and Execute. Experienced riders use this system to make safe decisions while riding.
